Decision path

Three gates replace six handoffs

Each phase combines related analysis and ends with a committee vote. The output of one gate becomes the constraint for the next.

Phase 1

Frame the Mandate

Agree on the world you are investing in and the rules you cannot break.

Phase 2

Build & Challenge

Turn the approved view into portfolios, then try to break them.

Phase 3

Defend the Recommendation

Make the recommendation visible, auditable, and defensible under pressure.

Four-person committee

Distinct ownership, shared accountability

Each member leads a workstream, but every member reviews, votes, signs the decision record, and answers questions across the full recommendation.

Committee seat

Committee Chair & Client Mandate Lead

Own the meeting process, client suitability, decision record, and integration across all three phases.

Committee seat

Markets & Economic Strategist

Own the 12-month macro thesis, scenario probabilities, data provenance, and transmission logic.

Committee seat

Portfolio Construction Lead

Own capital-market expectations, optimization, security selection, allocation, and implementation feasibility.

Committee seat

Risk, Controls & Challenge Lead

Own independent challenge, stress testing, hedge analysis, the AI audit, and mandate-breach escalation.

Project phases

Build the case in the order the committee needs it

Use the phase guides as the current assignment authority. Supporting technical guides may retain older filenames while the migration is staged.

Phase 1 · Mandate

Frame the Mandate

What must be true about markets and each client before we are willing to invest?

Approval gateApprove or revise the common market view and all three client mandates. Portfolio construction cannot begin until the vote and action items are recorded.

Market view

Read the historical data before using AI, compare the committee view with FactSet/FRED consensus, and build bull/base/bear scenarios.

Client mandate

Translate each client profile into RRTTLLU constraints, return targets, liquidity needs, and an explicit drawdown tripwire.

Conflict register

Surface tensions among return, risk, liquidity, taxes, legal restrictions, and unique circumstances before approving the mandate.

Open Phase 1 guide → Macro starter workbook XLSX Assigned client profiles PPTX

Phase 2 · Portfolio

Build & Challenge

Does each portfolio earn its place inside the client mandate after costs, constraints, and the bear case?

Approval gateApprove, revise, or reject each client portfolio. A failed tripwire cannot receive approval without a documented correction.

A · Capital-market expectations

Convert the market view into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and Solver constraints for base and bear cases.

B · Securities & implementation

Select and weight securities, document macro and client fit, and compare at least two risk-mitigation approaches.

C · Stress test & corrective action

Run the bear case, test the tripwire, quantify hedge effects, and document trades required to cure any breach.

Phase 3 · Decision

Defend the Recommendation

Can every committee member defend the same evidence-linked recommendation to the panel?

Approval gateIssue the final recommendation, record dissent or reservations, and defend the evidence. Every member must answer questions outside the workstream they led.

Decision memo

State the recommendation first, then connect the market view, client mandate, portfolio, and risk decision.

Technical exhibit book

Present the auditable evidence: scenarios, IPS constraints, allocations, securities, stress results, and sources.

Committee defense

Deliver a visual pitch, answer adversarial questions, and show that all four members understand the integrated decision.

Committee operating protocol

Every phase ends with a decision

Analysis becomes committee work only when the team challenges it, votes, and records what happens next.

Pre-read

Circulate the required evidence before the meeting. Every member reviews the full package.

Recommendation

The workstream lead states a clear recommendation and cites the evidence that supports it.

Independent challenge

The Risk, Controls & Challenge Lead presents the strongest counterargument or mandate risk.

Motion and vote

The Chair records approve, revise, or reject. All four members vote; ties require revision.

Decision record

Capture evidence reviewed, dissent or reservations, owners, and actions before the next gate.

AI rules of engagement

Use AI as a challenger, never as an unverified source

Log material prompts, summarize how the output affected the analysis, and identify the human-verified source used before any claim or number enters the committee record.

Permitted

Logic, debugging & challenge

Use AI to explain formulas, test reasoning, generate counterarguments, or surface missing risks.

Verify before use

Summaries, scenarios & estimates

Cross-check every factual claim and number against FactSet, FRED, SEC filings, or the team's workbook.

Not acceptable

Unverified decisions

Do not submit AI-generated allocations, risk metrics, citations, or client recommendations without human verification.

Canvas controls dates and submissions

Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission links, and course-grade weights.
